bhāradvāja.notes: Entry 05 is the clan article. It mentions the Vedic seer in passing. DN 13 names both Tārukkha’s pupil (5.1) and the ancient seer (13.1). MN 95 uses the name for Kāpaṭhika and the seer, and MN 99 for the seer and Subha, Todeyya’s son. MN 99 is a misplaced citation for 04. For sense 5, MN 7 names Sundarika Bhāradvāja and the speaker of Thag 2.29 rejoices at his son’s liberation. Neither passage identifies Dhanañjānī’s husband of SN 7.1. The bare name at the end of SN 7.2–4, 7.6–7 and 7.9–10 refers to the particular brahmin ordained in each discourse. MN 100 addresses Saṅgārava and SN 35.127 addresses Piṇḍola by their clan name. Entry 05 describes Kasi as a lay disciple, as at SN 7.11, while Snp 1.4 ends with his ordination and liberation. SN 35.133, Thag 2.30 and Thag 3.16 have chapter recaps. MN 75 identifies the fire-hut host in 06 and MN 74 concerns Dīghanakha. MN 116:6.26 has a further Bhāradvāja in Sujato where the app’s Pali reads dvārabhājo.

bhāvitatta.notes: DPPN counts two independent Buddhas with this name. MN 116:4.13 ends the prose list with Bhāvitatta, and 5.5–8 repeats the same names in the same order in verse. These two occurrences support one identification.

bilaṅgikabhāradvāja.notes: SN 7.4 names Bilaṅgika and says he stood silently in anger. The same page also picks up Asurindaka in SN 7.3 and Ahiṁsaka in SN 7.5.

bimbisāra.notes: The comparison of the king’s happiness with the Buddha’s occurs in MN 14:20–21. DPD points to MN 13 and the page also picks up MN 15. Thag 1.64:1.2 calls the father Paṇḍaraketu, the epithet DPPN gives for Bimbisāra.

bimbī.notes: Bimbī appears in the list of laywomen in AN 8.91–117. AN 8.89 and 8.90 are adjacent discourses.

bodhi.notes: MN 85:2.1 names Prince Bodhi as the owner of the Kokanada palace. MN 86 concerns Aṅgulimāla. MN 116:6.25 names an independent Buddha for whom this packet has no entry. The bodhiṁ at MN 26:25.1 and MN 85:49.2 is a place, rendered Bodhgaya. Thig 15.1:5.4 addresses the nun Bodhī. The packet misses Bodhi at MN 90:19.3 in the chapter recap of MN 85.

brahmadatta.notes: DN 19:36.13–16 lists Brahmadatta among the seven Bhāratas. The Jātaka king of sense 1 and the brahmin father of Kassapa named at DN 14:1.12.18 have no matching candidate. Thag 6.14:7.7 lists the elder of Thag 6.12 in the chapter recap. Sabbakāmi speaks the verses of Thag 6.14. Claude: The chapter summary at Thag 6.14:7.7 lists the poem of Thag 6.12, so it names Brahmadatta 04.

brahmadeva.notes: SN 6.3 names the monk and recounts his visit to his mother. The citation also lands in SN 6.2. SN 6.10:11.1 lists the title of SN 6.3 in the chapter recap.

brahmāyu.notes: MN 91:2.1 identifies the 120-year-old brahmin of Mithilā. MN 90 concerns King Pasenadi at Kaṇṇakatthala.

bāhiya.notes: AN 1.216 gives the bark-cloth epithet and AN 4.243:1.5 identifies Anuruddha’s pupil. SN 35.89 gives the lesson on the senses. Entry 03 also describes the mindfulness lesson in SN 47.15 but calls the identification of the two monks tentative. Each account ends with its pupil attaining arahantship and gives no detail linking him to the other occasion. SN 35.93:4.2 and SN 47.20:4.2 are chapter recaps. The mapped AN 1.198–208, AN 1.219–234, AN 4.242, SN 35.88 and SN 47.14 miss the respective episodes. Claude: The chapter summary at SN 35.93:4.2 recaps SN 35.89, so it names Bāhiya 03.

bāhumatī.notes: MN 7:20.5 names the river among bathing places. The surrounding verses reject the belief that bathing there washes away bad deeds.

bāhuraggi.notes: The app’s Pali has bāhuraggi in the same list of seven liberated in Aviha at SN 1.50:3.4 and SN 2.24:4.4. Sujato gives Bāhudanti and Bāhudantī respectively. The citation mapping picks up SN 1.49 and misses SN 2.24.

bārāṇasī.notes: AN 3.15 opens at Isipatana near Bārāṇasī. The page also picks up AN 3.14. Check the entry’s list of pilgrimage places. DN 16:5.8 identifies the birth site by the event, and Snp 3.11:5.3 locates the birth at Lumbinī. DPPN gives Kapilavatthu.

bāvarī.notes: Snp 5.1:31–35 names the sixteen pupils who set out after taking leave of Bāvarī. At 2.2 the app’s Pali has Aḷaka, as in DPPN, while Sujato gives Muḷaka. At 50–53 Ajita asks about the head and head-splitting before conveying Bāvarī’s greeting. DPPN reverses that sequence.

campā.notes: DN 19:36.8 names Campā as the city laid out for the Aṅgas. AN 7.52 and SN 8.11 place the Buddha there beside Gaggarā’s pond. The adjacent AN 7.51 and SN 8.10 also appear in the citation mapping.
